videos.title: Couples Therapist: We Lost the Ability to Fall in Love | Esther Perel
videos.description:
Esther Perel believes the friction you're trying to remove from dating is the exact thing that makes love possible.

In this clip, Esther Perel and Jay Shetty talk about why Gen Z is dating far less than the generations before them, and why the answer starts on the empty streets where kids used to play freely and learn to approach strangers, make rules, and make peace.

Esther argues we've built a contactless world. You don't have to leave the house to work, shop, eat, or be understood. So the whole training ground for relationships got skipped, and dating became a mountain you're expected to climb with no practice. She unpacks why 45% of young men have never approached a woman in public, why texting someone isn't the same as hearing their voice, and the "ambiguous loss" you feel when someone's sitting right next to you but scrolling.

Learn about the seven relational verbs Esther says you have to learn to conjugate, why every real love story is built around an obstacle, and the friend who almost spent five hours talking to an AI instead of the woman he ended up traveling Europe with.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
Join 900,000+ readers discovering how small daily shifts create big life change with my free newsletter. Subscribe https://news.jayshetty.me/subscribe

Chapters
0:00 — Why Gen Z is dating less
0:52 — The playground that taught you how to relate
2:27 — Why a screen can't give you real eye contact
4:29 — 45% of young men have never approached a woman
6:58 — Your first experiences, delayed by ten years
8:22 — Connected everywhere, lonely everywhere
9:34 — The friction that teaches you to really listen
10:33 — Why you're scared of being screenshotted
12:40 — How to build connection offline
14:31 — Ambiguous loss: here but not here
15:36 — No love story without an obstacle

videos.title: The AI content machine that turns ideas into posts that don't sound like slop | Alex Lieberman
videos.description:
Alex Lieberman co-founded Morning Brew in college and grew it into one of the most-read business newsletters in the world before selling it to Business Insider. Now he’s the co-founder and co-managing partner of Tenex. In this episode, Alex explains why distribution is becoming a durable moat, why founders and teams need to “climb Cringe Mountain,” and how he rebuilt his content process around AI without letting it produce generic slop. He walks us through every step of his Content Machine live: an Oracle that scans internal systems and the internet for content spikes, an interview panel that pulls out his real ideas, voice and style files that keep drafts sounding like him, an editorial council that scores and revises posts, and a lessons loop that learns from his feedback.

*What you’ll learn:*
1. Why the blank page is the biggest friction point in content creation, and how an AI Oracle eliminates it
2. How to map your current workflow before you add any AI
3. How Alex built a six-step Content Machine in Claude that goes from idea spike to publishable post
4. Why the interview step (not the drafting step) is where AI slop actually comes from
5. How to codify your voice in a Markdown file so an AI drafts in your register, not the internet’s average
6. Why your employees are your most underleveraged marketing channel right now
7. How the Tenex Creator Cup turned content creation into a team sport with a $5,000 prize pool

*Brought to you by:*
Firecrawl—Power AI agents with clean web data: https://firecrawl.dev/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=partner&utm_campaign=how_i_ai
Customer.io—Build customer engagement campaigns from a single prompt: https://www.customer.io/howiai

*In this episode, we cover:*
(00:00) Introduction to Alex Lieberman
(02:35) Why Alex built a content machine

(09:00) Mapping the workflow from scratch
(13:24) The six-step Content Machine setup
